title: Checkpoint composition does not yet fold group verdicts with the verdict semigroup
why: Card W45-AUDIT-CHECKPOINTS, running concurrently, adds `.qo` checkpoints with divide-and-conquer composition. Language spec §L21.2 states that a group verdict over checkpoints composes with the same join, and `qcore_schemas::verdict` exposes it (`Verdict::fold`, `ReasonedVerdict::fold`, `Chain` with `ChainKind::UnitGroup`); this card did not edit the checkpoint modules. DISCHARGE: the checkpoint compose calls `qcore_schemas::verdict` for every group verdict, with a test that a composed group equals the fold of its members' verdicts and that a `Pending` member keeps the group from `Safe`.

title: No trusted-core certificate checker exists for a user-contract checker plugin's Safe claim
why: The firewall counts a plugin's `Safe` only with a certificate the registry issues from a trusted-core `WitnessChecker` replay. `quirin-audit` registers none for the `quirin.user-contract-check.v1` task, so every plugin `Safe` it sees is `Pending` (`plugin-claim-uncertified`, QP008 or QP016); the certified row is exercised only through the library route with a test double of a checker. DISCHARGE: a versioned trusted-core checker for a precisely scoped user-contract claim, with independently replayable evidence, positive, negative and mutation tests, and the command line registering it.

title: No trusted-core counterexample checker exists, so no plugin Unsafe is validated
why: `qcore_verifier_host::plugin_firewall::CounterexampleChecker` is the hook a plugin's `Unsafe` needs; no production implementation exists and `quirin-audit` passes none, so every plugin `Unsafe` is `Pending`. The validated row is exercised only at the host with a test double. DISCHARGE: a trusted-core counterexample checker for a named capability, validating a witness against the core's obligation inventory, with mutation tests, and a report stating how a validated plugin `Unsafe` is presented (provisional, never an upstream defect).

title: Checker plugins and user load paths reach `quirin-audit current` and `contracts` only
why: `user_plugins::run` is hooked into `CurrentAudit::with_contracts` and `NoBuildAudit::with_plugin_checkers`. The configured `quirin-audit CONFIG.json` route and the corpus arbiter (`cycle19_fluent_bit_libraries_audit`) select contracts by manifest and never read a user load path, so a checker binding cannot reach them; a caller of the gateway API applies the environment it is given. DISCHARGE: an inventory of the verdict-publishing routes, each running the bindings of the load path it resolves or refusing one it cannot, with a test per route.

title: The callee chain reads applied contracts from the control-flow graph's contract calls
why: `user_plugins::fold_unit` joins a bound contract's verdict into every function whose CFG holds a `LegacyInstruction::ContractCall` (or an admitted nested call) of it. Six call shapes (assignment, initialisation, return, condition, discarded cast, expression operand) were probed to lower to `ContractCall`; a contracted call applied through any other instruction would not carry its link, and a refused call applies no contract and already leaves its function `Unknown`. DISCHARGE: the gateway records the contracts each function applied as part of its summary (or a census proving every applied contract is a `ContractCall`), with a test per lowering route.

title: A checker plugin's task borrows `parameter_mode_respected` for a whole-contract claim
why: The core-derived task for a binding has one obligation per bound function with property `parameter_mode_respected`, the closest existing `ObligationProperty`; what a user's checker actually checks is not in the closed vocabulary, so the claim's scope is the contract as a whole rather than a named property. DISCHARGE: a dedicated obligation property (a schema change) naming the checked claim, carried into the task digest, with the firewall and the report unchanged otherwise.

title: Checker packages run under the host's default execution profile
why: A binding names a package, and `ProcessProvider::from_package` runs it under the default profile (`unenforced-legacy`: process-group containment, deadline and output bound, no declared rlimits or confinement); the sidecar records the profile and limits. A user load path cannot yet request `linux-rlimit-v1` or `linux-confined-v1`. DISCHARGE: a binding field selecting the profile (and a confinement policy), refusing one the host cannot enforce, with the refusal tested.
